title: A SysML Modeling Strategy to Digitalize FAR 23 Substantiation Methods
content: This study proposes a methodology for digitalizing aircraft certification processes under FAR 23, Subpart C, of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), through a model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approach utilizing the Systems Modeling Language (SysML). The proposed framework encodes regulatory requirements and substantiation methods. Consensus standards documents, such as the ones published and maintained by ASTM International, provide the main source for these methods. The encoded requirements and methods are exported and parsed into structured data formats and used to inform a Python code suite that performs the substantiation calculations of the modeled paragraphs. The methodology is demonstrated across three representative aircraft architectures. Key outputs include automated generation of flight envelopes, balancing loads, and powerplant load calculations. The framework is evaluated against four research questions: encoding, correctness, consistency with independent data, and behavior with faulty input. Verification against the definitions of the standard and the equilibrium equations revealed and corrected three defects in the balancing-load calculation; the engine torque, side load, and normal load agree within 1% with non-public manufacturer data, and the larger differences are traced to differing assumptions. The study is a proof of concept whose practical benefit remains to be evaluated by certification practitioners.
